purpose: Human-centred Pockitle article for weddings, conferences and classrooms. Preserve emotional intent and product truth, not English sentence structure.
globalRules: Write as a native editorial article, not a literal translation.
Preserve the human arc: important moment -> risk of exclusion -> second reading route -> participation -> honest limits.
Adapt wedding, academic and classroom details to what feels natural in the target culture while keeping the same ethical point.
Localize illustrative language examples. Never carry an unrelated example language through mechanically.
When the article contrasts source and reading languages, use the target language as one of the reading-language examples where natural.
Do not invent product capabilities. Keep one fixed spoken source language, original captions plus up to three translations, browser/QR audience access, and current limits.
Do not claim professional CART, interpreting replacement, official transcript, certified accessibility or legal/educational compliance.
Do not promise singing, music-led captioning, sustained-overlap reliability or automatic source-language switching.
Prefer culturally natural names, family relations, education terms and event vocabulary over literal English calques.
Do not translate English-language test references mechanically where they are culturally odd; replace them with a locally familiar second-language proficiency context or general wording.
Keep quoted vow wording natural for the locale; it may be rewritten rather than literally translated.
